# SuperToolkit

> A credential broker for agents: the agent asks for an effect by name and never holds, reads or receives the credential that causes it.

SuperToolkit (`stk`) runs on your own machine, on Linux and macOS. A broker holds credentials in a process the agent cannot read; clients are started with `HTTPS_PROXY` pointing at it and a placeholder (`stk:ref:<service>:v1`) where their token would be, and the broker substitutes, signs, mints, refreshes or exchanges on the wire. Policy is one committed file with safe defaults: a read is agent-callable, a write needs approval. Every request is recorded in an audit ledger that holds a fingerprint of the credential, never its value. Agents use it over MCP (`stk mcp`, four tools). Apache-2.0, installed with a checksum-verified installer.

## Docs

- [What it is](https://docs.supertoolkit.dev/): the product and the one invariant
- [Install](https://docs.supertoolkit.dev/install/): the installer, or build from source
- [Limitations](https://docs.supertoolkit.dev/limitations/): what it does not do, and why
